Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
With more and more of the population gaining accesses to internet due to the roll of fibre, and free WIFI hotspots aross cities ,are children being protected from accessing obscene content on the we

Unique Selling Point:
The city of Joburg has laid out 1000 KM of fiber across the city, which equates to 85 Free internet hotspots across the city at 500 MB/day per person, mainly targeted at Job seekers and students, But is the free access being used for its intended purpose and are there contingencies in places to protect minors from accessing obscene material of the internet- be it through unsolicited pornographic material pop-ups, porn through social media platforms like Twitter.
We will also explore the protection of minors through specific legislation- The Cyber Crimes Bill for example.
WE will also explore the psychological effects of minors being exposed to pornographic material and the proliferation of child pornography.

Case Study:
Vox pops free WIFI users in Joburg

Script:


Banana Bread Link: We all had to adjust to life under lockdown. With nowhere to go and the novelty of baking banana bread wearing off, we mostly turned to the internet for an escape, we connected with friends virtually and it’s easy entertainment for the kids.

VO: Working and learning from home has seen many households improve their internet connectivity, getting faster wifi and upgrading their internet connectivity device.While the internet is a useful tool, sexual predators have also had more ready access to children, teens and young adults.

Upsound Richard Frost: [03:44]Sexual predators out there entice children to post things they would not normally do, pictures that put them in compromising positions, that can be used in child pornography sites.

V/O Cyber security expert Richard Frost warns that sexual predators are becoming bolder online.

Upsound Richard Frost: 07:53In South Africa it’s becoming more and more common and if you look at just last year there was quite a few predators that were actually arrested, South African police and the FBI working closely together. 08:33the common point is the social media or online.

V/O Within the South African Police Service’s Family Violence, Child Protection and Sexual Offence’s unit, the Serial and Electronic Crime Investigations Unit or SECI has been making inroads, specialising in Cybercrime and child pornography.

13:56 A lot of the take downs that have been happening recently of cyber predators have had some involvement in the dark web and a lot of it again is in South Africa.

V/O: In major operations in Gauteng, SECI cracked down on sexual predators, arresting five individuals for the possession of explicit child abuse content.

V/O: The Economist Intelligence Unit’s Out of the Shadow Index ranks South Africa as 16th out of 60 countries for responsiveness to child sexual exploitation.

V/O: While legislation like the Cybercrimes Bill aims to give law enforcement agencies like SECI the power to investigate, search, access and seize digital information even on platforms like Whatsapp, high-level implementation and crackdown lag behind.

VO: Clinical Psychologist Navlika Ratangee says the taboo surrounding child sexual images, helps to keep potential threats under a veil of secrecy.

Navlika 23:17 One of the questions that get asked frequently is do people openly disclose that they are interested in child pornography, and I wouldn’t say that it is something commonly disclosed upfront As I said people usually talk about the stress they feel upfront, that’s usually the first layer and then in unpacking that, once there’s a rapport, we might understand that it has manifested in the viewing of pornography and only in much deeper levels would it then be disclosed around child pornography in specific.but that really is a sort of a whole new boall game in terms of how that is dealt with. But I think what it does raise as well is the whole issue of what’s known as the AAA engine and that is around why we’re seeing this increase in pornography is there’s an increase in accessibility, in affordability, and there’s an increase in anonymity.


V/) In the past pornography was primarily available in more traditional forms of media Ratangee warns that with connectivity to world wide web through the smartphones, porn is increasingly accessable.

Braamlink: Gone are the days of strict age restriction for porn today you can …


2nd :2:35 - 02:53 ( Girl with the braids )
VO: Younger and more impressionable children are using smartphones, making them susceptible to potential predators, Ratangee says whilst parents can not always monitor what kids are doing online, she stresses developing transparent conversations on having an online presence .

Navlika 27;03 it’s important to create that open dialogue and open conversation around the dangers of the internet broadly speaking so it’s not just pornography there’s so many other things that become dangerous from a child’t perspective as well.


Masa[5:13] Question My concern is when kids are posting bikini pics , innocent fun and that picture is taken by a stranger if they have a public account.

Upsound Richard Frost : you want to make sure that the settings are private[.5:51 your children should only allow access to people that they know that they’ve met face to face, if they don’t that person don’t allow, if they have an uncle that keeps asking you about your bikini pics there’s a problem there as well so even people that you know could be a problem. 05:05 - 05;13 If certain conversations are making the children feel uncomfortable or making them feel different from what they would normally feel, tell them to back off close and speak to your parents.



V/ O Whilst the internet and social media allows us to connect and share details of our lives, recent trends are pointing to the fact that the danger can be right under your nose

Promos 11 seconds :


As livestreaming and smartphones allow children to upload images of themselves and meet strangers online…how does South Africa protect its children against child sexual abuse online?

As social media platforms become more accessible for younger children and teens, sexual predators on the lookout are becoming bolder online. How safe are your children on their smartphones?

As recent international trends show an increase in child sexual abuse material online, what is put in place to protect South Africa‘s children?
